key_insight: A two-flexible-plate Poiseuille-flow channel can trigger a critical-layer instability of structural-acoustic wall modes, with symmetric modes becoming convectively unstable above a Mach-number threshold while antisymmetric modes remain protected by a mid-plane pressure node.
engineering_relevance: The result helps predict when compliant ducts or channels may amplify acoustic/structural oscillations under flow, informing the design of quieter and more stable aeroacoustic and fluid-structure systems.
method: Closed-form O(M) correction for coupled wavenumbers using a Fredholm solvability argument.
Dispersion and stability analysis of symmetric vs antisymmetric wall modes with critical-layer physics.
Briggs-Bers classification plus spatial and temporal growth-rate calculations.
evidence_signal: Three independent numerical schemes agree to within 10^-9, and the analytic low-Mach correction matches numerical differentiation across three shear profiles.
watch_item: The instability is specific to compliant walls and appears above a critical Mach number, so rigid-wall intuition or low-Mach approximations may miss the onset condition and mode-dependent behavior.
paper_title: A critical-layer instability of structural acoustic wall modes in a two-flexible-plate channel with Poiseuille flow: closed-form low-Mach corrections and parity-protected absorption
